basic_info.headline: Software Engineer at Plaid
basic_info.about:
👋 nice to see ya! Quick elevator pitch: I'm a driven software engineer who's spent a lot of time working on internal platform tooling with enough devops experience to be dangerous. I build highly observable, resilient systems that tend to stay healthy and require relatively little maintenance as they scale.

I'm known for bringing an enthusiastic and infectious personality to the teams I work with, while creating a positive space that allows everyone to perform their best work.

When I'm not working, I'm likely in the mountains, racing bicycles, or skiing - depending on the season. Being a good stuarts to the planet and humanity are critically important and I hope to leave a positive influence on everyone around me. Onward!

location.full: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States

experience.title: Software Engineer
experience.description:
Responsible for keeping our bank integration infrastructure alive and providing tooling so that an ~80 engineer organization can stay on top of the health of their integrations. We support 12,000 institutions, investment platforms, and other financial providers in the US, Canada, and Europe. Each geography has unique uptime baselines, providing us a constant challenge of managing alert fatigue with quality and alert usefulness.

When not wrangling PromQL queries to keep our integrations engineers happy, our team ensures our enormous Kubernetes clusters stay healthy, in conjunction with our primary infrastructure team. They own the Kubernetes infra, we own everything on top of that. Due to a number of complex factors, we frequently maintain state across pods and have spent countless hours wrangling obscure networking-level bugs. We also manage custom deployment logic for our largest ~6000 pod service and can deploy it dozens of times a day.

I have owned significant reliability efforts that cut across our stack, constantly pushing for improved observability and service resiliency.

I volunteered our team to be a guinea pig for Plaid's original migration to Kubernetes from ECS. We learned a lot, and realized it certainly takes a while to move large, business critical services between clustering methodologies. Especially with 0 tolerance for downtime. We survived to tell the tale.

Other teams know me for being a significant culture carrier for both my team and the entire engineering org.

Generous quotes from coworkers include: 
"Austin is also a serious driver of personality of the team."
"He is very motivated to solve problems for other teams."
"The first to praise engineers when they accomplish something especially difficult, which is not something to be taken for granted."

SEO appeasement: NodeJS, Typescript, GoLang, ELK / Kibana, CloudFormation, plus everything listed previously, except Java.

experience.title: Software Engineer
experience.description:
Built and shipped the next iteration of our event-driven notification microservice. This service handled the events from thousands of medical facilities around the country, from patient checkins to prescription notifications. We'd use this data to notify care providers of time-sensitive issues for their patients. Significant performance improvements were made in addition to complex new event evaluation criteria, frequently at a moment's notice for important customers.

I enjoyed learning about the intricacies of the medical world. Also, I was the two-time reigning Magic The Gathering draft tournament champion, without any previous play experience. Certainly transferrable engineering skills.

We were mostly a Java shop. Most business logic was in a monolith, with significant new development in a microservice architecture.

To appease the crawlers: Springboot, Gradle, Docker, Angular, NodeJS, Prometheus, Grafana, Splunk, MySQL, and probably a few others.

mediums

• Train current and new employees, teaching the fundamentals and best practices of
successful sound design

projects.name: Adam & Reba for MUSG Campaign - Content Creator
projects.description: Created the photo and video content for a MUSG (Marquette student government) election campaign. Shot short platform-specific video segments for targeting advertisement on Facebook and Instagram. All deliverables were turned around within days of shoot, for immediately posting to social media.

projects.name: Kappa Delta Marquette Recruitment Film
projects.description: Worked with social media and outreach team of the Kappa Delta sorority at Marquette to produce their annual recruitment film. Filmed in multiple locations throughout the city, in addition to interviews. Executed the ideas provided by the chapter, and staying within the stringent guidelines provided by the university.
